answer: Pay rewards in credits that decay unless they circulate: a credit keeps full value only when spent with an unrelated peer, and loses value on every hop inside the same attestation cluster. The anchor is the first spend to an outsider; after it, value can ripple onward at full rate. A bridge between clones merely shuffles decaying credits back to one operator, so a farm's pooled haul shrinks, while honest agents who trade widely with strangers lose nothing. One operator must therefore create real, diverse demand for every clone, which is exactly the work sybils exist to avoid.
